content:
# Crew

Crew is a team work tracker with organizations, projects, issues and activity.

## Issues and discussion

Open a project's Issues page to filter work by text, workflow state, assignee, priority and label. Create or edit the full issue record: Markdown description, status, priority, assignee, fractional estimate, due date, parent and labels. Project numbers are sequential and never reused after deletion. Parent cycles and cross-project labels/statuses are rejected with field errors. Archived projects are read-only. Project label management supports names and colors, and updates issue views and search event snapshots.

Issue detail provides Markdown rendering, parent and child links, safe comment previews, a project-visible mention picker, author/admin comment edits, and blocks/duplicates/relates controls. Directed relations display their inverse meanings on the other issue; symmetric relates links cannot duplicate in reverse. Raw HTML is escaped and executable link schemes are inactive. Mentions resolve only to people who can read the project. Guests read and comment only on granted projects; issue changes require member access.

Use `crew issue help` for the full issue CLI. Typical commands are `issue create PROJECT --title TEXT`, `issue list PROJECT --label ID --query TEXT`, `issue edit ISSUE --estimate 3.5 --due 2028-02-29`, `issue comment ISSUE --body TEXT`, and `issue relate ISSUE --target ISSUE --kind blocks`. Nullable fields accept `none`; deletion requires `--yes`. Description/comment file inputs avoid shell quoting. [Issue API, event schema and CLI](docs/api-work-issues.md) documents every field, permission, pagination shape, mention form and relation meaning.

## Demo data

Run `npm run seed` to create the idempotent Crew Demo organization, Delivery team, DEMO project, three issues, and accounts `owner@crew.demo`, `member@crew.demo`, and `guest@crew.demo`. Each demo account uses password `crew-demo-password-2026`. These are local demonstration credentials; keep the data private. Re-running seed preserves existing demo project/issue edits and avoids duplicate records.

## Boards, sprints and files

Open a project’s Board to drag issues between or within ordered workflow columns. Every card also has a keyboard move menu; select several cards to edit status, assignee and labels atomically. Open Sprints to create a dated goal, preview scope additions, start one active sprint, review the daily points/issue-count burndown, and complete it with an explicit carry-over target. Historical sprint results remain fixed. Issue pages include streaming attachments with upload progress/cancel, the configured size limit, SHA-256 details, exact downloads and delete controls.

Use `crew board help` and `crew sprint help` for all board, bulk, planning and streaming file commands. `crew board attach ISSUE --file PATH` streams a file; `crew board download ATTACHMENT --output PATH` verifies size and SHA-256 while writing a new file. Runtime blobs are under `CREW_DATA_DIR/attachments`; back up them with crew.sqlite while the service is stopped. The protected API and CLI enforce the same role/project/token rules.

## Project planning

Open Projects to create an organization project, configure its key/name/description, and edit its ordered workflow. Status IDs remain stable during rename/reorder; move issues before removing an occupied status. Workflows require todo and done categories. Owners/admins manage projects; members collaborate; guests read only granted projects. Archive hides a project from the current-project list and protects issue edits; restore it from the archived list. Numbered project keys remain fixed so issue references stay meaningful.

Use `crew project create --org ID --key TEAM --name "Team roadmap"`, `project list`, `project show ID`, `project update ID --description TEXT`, `project archive ID`, `project restore ID`, `project workflow ID`, or `project workflow-set ID --file workflow.json`. Project deletion requires `project delete ID --yes`. See [Work API and CLI](docs/api-work.md) for request shapes, cursor lists, workflow files, permissions and lifecycle behavior.


## Setup

Use Node 22.23.1 and npm 10.9.8. Run `npm ci --fetch-retries=0 --fetch-timeout=60000 --no-audit --no-fund`, `npm run build`, `npm run prepare-tests`, and `npm test`. Start with `npm start` and open http://localhost:4100.

## Configuration

`PORT` defaults to 4100. `CREW_DATA_DIR` defaults to ./data and contains crew.sqlite plus attachment blobs. Set `CREW_SECRET`, `CREW_BASE_URL`, and `CREW_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (default 25 MiB). Back up the entire data folder while Crew is stopped. Keep it private. The diagnostic default secret must be replaced for deployment.

## Packages and scripts

shared holds validation, schemas and query logic; server owns HTTP/SQLite; web is Preact built with esbuild; cli is the `crew` executable. Each package has `npm test`; web also has `npm run build`. Root scripts are build, prepare-tests, test, start, seed and smoke. Tests run on temporary databases through actual HTTP.

## Authentication and CLI

Web sessions use httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies. Cookie mutations require X-Crew-Request: 1. `crew login --url URL --email EMAIL --password PASSWORD` stores a restricted config file. `crew whoami --json` reads it; `--config` chooses another file. Personal API tokens are supplied with --token or CREW_TOKEN. CREW_URL overrides the configured API URL.

## API and permissions

See [API](docs/api.md) and [architecture](docs/architecture.md). People supplies the common organization/project permission service, work emits changes, insight consumes them. Lists return items/nextCursor with limit 1–200.

## Filter language

The insight lane documents its boolean filter grammar and examples after integration.

## Known limitations

This is a diagnostic build, not a released service. No mail is sent: invitations, resets and digests live in the protected local outbox. Production TLS and external backups are operator concerns. No test skips are currently declared.

## Organizations and teams

Open Organizations to create a workspace, rename it, manage its roster and roles, and create teams. Owners and admins manage access; only owners manage other owners, and every organization must retain an owner. Members can collaborate across organization projects. Guests can read organization people and teams, and read/comment only in explicitly granted projects. Removing membership removes team access and project grants. Team membership does not grant access outside the organization. See [People API and permission service](docs/api-people.md) for endpoints, exact scopes, project access methods and the single local outbox schema. Invitation, local outbox and account-security pages support one-use recipient-bound invitations, session revocation and password change/reset. Account security revokes other sessions and API tokens when passwords change; reset revokes all. CREW_SECRET signs purpose-bound credentials and must remain stable across restarts/backups. Personal Tokens offers scope selection, expiry, private copy-once credentials and immediate revocation. Organization and account Audit pages filter persisted sanitized security changes by actor/type/target/action/date. Lists have Next/Previous browsing, and destructive access changes ask for confirmation. Use `crew org --help`, `crew team --help`, `crew invite --help` and `crew token --help` for real administration commands; removal/revocation requires `--yes`. `crew token create --name Automation --scopes self:read,org:read --days 30 --save-to PRIVATE_FILE` stores a 0600 Bearer-token config. Account outbox links are available only through browser-session authentication. See the People API for endpoints, role/scope policies, signing, reset recovery and data/backup locations.

# People API and access contract

All paths use `/api/v1`. Sessions require `X-Crew-Request: 1` for mutations. Lists accept `limit` and `cursor` and return `items,nextCursor`.

`GET/POST /orgs` lists organizations for the signed-in account or creates one with `{name}`. Creation assigns its creator owner. `GET/PATCH /orgs/:orgId` reads or renames. `GET/POST /orgs/:orgId/members` lists or adds an existing account with `{userId,role}`. `PATCH/DELETE /orgs/:orgId/members/:userId` changes role or removes membership. At least one owner must remain; only owners appoint or manage owners. Removing membership also removes team memberships and project guest grants.

`GET/POST /orgs/:orgId/teams`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /teams/:teamId` use `{name,description}`. `GET/POST /teams/:teamId/members` and `DELETE /teams/:teamId/members/:userId` manage existing organization members. Duplicate names and memberships return 409.

Owners/admins administer organizations, people and projects. Members can read organizations and read/write project work. Guests can read their organization roster and teams, and only read/comment on specifically granted projects. Guest search/activity is restricted to those projects. `GET/POST /projects/:projectId/guests` and `DELETE /projects/:projectId/guests/:userId` require project administration. Post body is `{userId}` for an organization guest.

## Stable service for other lanes

People registers first. Use `ctx.permissions.assertOrg(req,orgId,permission='org:read')`, `assertProject(req,projectId,permission='project:read')`, `assertSelf(req,userId=req.user.id,permission='self:read')` and `scope(req,permission)`. Assertion methods throw stable AppErrors. `assertOrg` returns the membership; `assertProject` returns the raw project. `membership(userId,orgId)` returns a raw membership or null. `canOrg(userId,orgId,permission)` and `canProject(userId,projectId,permission)` return booleans; `projectIds(userId,orgId)` returns accessible project ids. Booleans do not check token scopes: route handlers must call `scope` as well. Projects have `projects.id,projects.org_id`; guests use people's `project_guests(project_id,user_id,created_at)`. Project deletion should remove guest rows.

Permission names: self:read/self:write, org:read/org:manage, members:manage, teams:manage, invites:manage, audit:read, project:read/project:write/project:manage, issue:write, comment:write, attachment:write, insight:read/insight:write, export:read, import:write. Tokens may name exact permissions, namespace wildcards such as project:*, or *. A scope never expands the user's role or project access.

## Shared outbox

One table `outbox(id,org_id,user_id,kind,to_email,subject,text_body,payload_json,created_at,sent_at)` stores invite/reset/digest rows. `org_id` and `user_id` may be null. Call `ctx.enqueueOutbox({orgId,userId,kind,toEmail,subject,textBody,payload})`, returning camelCase row metadata and parsed payload. Payloads for invite/reset contain the one-use link; digest payloads are insight-owned. This local outbox is the delivery surface; no external mail service is configured. Protect link contents as credentials. Do not create a second outbox table.

## Invitations and account security

`GET/POST /orgs/:orgId/invitations` requires invites:manage. POST accepts `{email,role,expiresInHours,projectIds}`. Expiry defaults to 168 hours, range 1–720. Only owners invite owners. Only guest invitations accept projectIds, all in the invitation organization. Pending duplicate invitations and existing memberships return 409. GET supports `state=pending|accepted|revoked|expired|all` before cursor pagination. `DELETE /invitations/:id` revokes a pending invitation. A revoked, accepted or expired link cannot be used again.

`POST /invitations/preview` accepts `{token}` and returns its pending recipient/organization/role. `POST /invitations/accept` requires self:write and the authenticated account's exact normalized email; it atomically adds the invited membership and guest project grants. The existing account's role cannot be overwritten. The link is delivered only to the single shared outbox; invitation responses expose metadata without credentials.

`GET /me/outbox?kind=invite|reset|digest` requires a browser session plus self:read and returns messages addressed to the current account only. `GET /orgs/:orgId/outbox` requires invites:manage and exposes that organization's invitation messages only. Treat outbox link text/payload as private credentials. No external email delivery is configured.

`GET /auth/sessions` requires self:read and lists unexpired sessions with current, lastUsedAt, expiresAt and userAgent metadata. `DELETE /auth/sessions/:id` requires self:write and revokes only a session owned by the caller; deleting the current one clears its cookie. `POST /auth/sessions/revoke-others` with `{}` revokes all other sessions.

`POST /auth/password/change` takes `{currentPassword,password}` and requires self:write, verifies the existing scrypt hash, retains the current browser session, and revokes every other session, personal API token and outstanding reset link. API-token callers must sign in again afterwards. New passwords require 10–1024 characters and must differ from the current password.

`POST /auth/password/reset/request` accepts `{email}` and always returns the same 202 response for known/unknown valid addresses. Known accounts receive a one-hour link through the shared outbox; a new request invalidates older links. `POST /auth/password/reset` accepts `{token,password}`. It is public, uses the one-use link, and revokes all sessions and API tokens. Sign in again after reset. Invalid, expired and used links return 422; concurrent consumption returns 409. An administrator operating this local diagnostic service can retrieve a reset message from private runtime data when the account has no active session.

Sessions, invite/reset links and personal API tokens use random 256-bit credentials signed with CREW_SECRET using HMAC-SHA256 and distinct purpose tags. Database lookup stores SHA256 only. Verification checks purpose/signature before lookup, so changing CREW_SECRET invalidates existing credentials. Keep CREW_SECRET stable across restarts and restore it alongside the private data backup. Outbox intentionally stores delivery links until an operator removes private runtime data. Password hashes, link credentials and plaintext tokens never enter domain events or audit summaries.

## Personal API tokens and security audit

`POST /tokens` accepts `{name,scopes,expiresInDays}` and requires self:write. Name is at most 100 characters. Choose exact permissions, known namespace wildcards or `*`; expiry is 1–365 days or null for no expiry. Defaults grant self:read, org:read, project:read and insight:read. Creation returns `{personalToken,token}`; save the plaintext token then, because GET never repeats it. Tokens store only SHA256 lookup hashes. A token may mint only a subset of its own scopes. `GET /tokens?state=all|active|expired|revoked` requires self:read and returns metadata/scopes/state/lastUsedAt. `DELETE /tokens/:id` requires self:write and revokes a caller-owned token immediately. Expired/revoked/signed-with-another-secret tokens return 401. An invalid Bearer credential never falls back to a cookie.

`ctx.authenticateToken(plaintext)` returns `{kind:'token',tokenId,user,scopes}` after signature, hash, expiry and revoke checks. Authentication uses the same users, sessions, publicUser and hashToken helpers as browser login. Every subsequent handler must check both scope and current role/project access; a wildcard cannot make a guest an administrator. Account outbox links require browser authentication even if a token has self:read. Organization invitation outbox access requires invites:manage.

`GET /orgs/:orgId/audit` requires audit:read and administrator/owner membership. Filters are actorId, entityType, entityId, projectId, action, from and to (inclusive ISO timestamps), plus limit/cursor. Cross-organization project filters are rejected. `GET /me/audit` requires self:read and returns only the account's own security actions with no organization context. Persisted security types include organization/membership, team/roster, invitation, session, user login/password/reset and personal token creation/revocation; project guest grants are included. Summaries allow only explicit identity/role/scope/lifecycle fields. No arbitrary request, password hash, token hash, plaintext token or delivery payload is persisted into audit. The audit event subscriber is removed during ctx.cleanup before server drain.

## Administration web and CLI

Organizations, member rosters, teams and team rosters offer opaque-cursor Next/Previous pages; the team member picker also browses the complete roster. Destructive membership/team/invite/session/token controls require deliberate confirmation. Forms retain input on errors and show field details. Organization tabs open Members, Teams, Invitations and Audit. Account security opens Sessions/Password, Tokens, personal Audit and Outbox. Token creation shows a private copy-once credential with an explicit hide action. Invitation pages distinguish pending/expired/revoked/accepted; accepted/reset links cannot be replayed.

Use `crew org --help`, `crew team --help`, `crew invite --help` and `crew token --help` for full commands and options. `org` supports list/show/create/rename/members/add/role/remove, guest project grants and filtered audit. `team` supports list/show/create/update/delete/members/add/remove. `invite` supports list/create/preview/accept/revoke/outbox. `token` supports list/create/revoke. Lists preserve items/nextCursor and support --limit/--cursor. Destructive commands require --yes. `invite accept --link URL` requires the invited account; --credential supplies the token directly when needed. `token create --name TOOL --scopes self:read,org:read --days 30 --save-to FILE` writes a private 0600 CLI config containing the token; without --save-to creation prints it once. `CREW_TOKEN` or --token uses Bearer authentication; --config selects a stored config. Do not put secrets in command history on a shared machine.

People data persists in `CREW_DATA_DIR/crew.sqlite` alongside the shared outbox and sanitized audit. Attachment bytes remain in the work-owned attachments directory. Stop Crew and back up the entire data directory plus CREW_SECRET configuration; restore both together. CLI configuration defaults to ~/.config/crew/config.json and is private. Acceptance credentials/configs live only under private data/ and are excluded from production source.

## Current route audit boundary

The people.3 implementation review covers all integrated auth/people/project/workflow/issue/label/comment/relation/board/bulk/sprint/attachment routes. Project/issue/relation lists filter guest access before cursor pagination; stream upload checks access both before receiving and before publishing. HTTP tests prove guest and scoped-token denials for these routes, and scripts/checks/people.mjs audits every registered API route's unauthenticated boundary using a real temporary HTTP server. Insight is not integrated at this source head: its search, activity, notifications, saved filters, dashboards, export/import and live SSE still require a successor role/project/scope audit. The current SSE route returns 503 after self authentication and is not a claim of live insight behavior.

# Architecture and lane contracts

The monorepo has @crew/shared, @crew/server, @crew/web and @crew/cli. All packages are ES modules. Node SQLite is synchronous. Never await inside transaction(fn). Migrations export up(db) and run in filename order once. Ranges: 001 L0; 100–199 people; 200–249 W1; 250–299 W2; 300–349 I1; 350–399 I2.

Server lane modules export registerRoutes(ctx) from modules/<lane>/routes.js. ctx contains app, db (raw DatabaseSync), bus, config, requireAuth, asyncRoute, paginate, pagination, transaction(fn), id(), now(). People registers first and assigns ctx.permissions and ctx.authenticateToken(token). Authentication runs per request and sees those hooks. req.user is {id,email,name,createdAt,updatedAt}; req.auth is {kind:'session',sessionId,user} or people-defined token identity with kind:'token', scopes. All protected handlers use requireAuth then the people authorization service. Document that service's stable methods in people API docs before work begins.

Domain mutations call bus.emit({actorId,orgId,projectId,entityType,entityId,action,before,after,time}). bus adds UUID and default UTC time. Consumers are synchronous and return promptly; all event state persists through SQLite, with no second outbox or auth system. Storage column names use snake_case; public API uses camelCase. Insight subscribes after work registration, before requests begin. Register shutdown callbacks in ctx.cleanups; mark ctx.sseRegistered=true when replacing SSE.

Web lane pages/<lane>/routes.jsx exports routes [{path,component}] and navigation [{path,label}]. Hash route params are decoded; page props are params,query,user,api,store,navigate. Components include Page,Field,Button,Notice,Empty,Loading,DataTable,useLoad in components/ui.jsx. API helper get/post/patch/put/delete sends CSRF header and reports stable errors. Add focused CSS under styles and import from lane routes if required.

CLI commands/<lane>.js exports commands, an object keyed by group name. Each async command receives {command,args,options,client,configFile,print}. args are positional arguments after group; options maps --name values and --json booleans. client offers get/post/patch/delete/request. Return output via print(value). Reuse client query helper and output formatting. CLI dispatch automatically loads implemented lanes.

Tests live outside src/bin. Server test/helpers.js exports testServer() with ctx,url,agent(),close(). agent() returns request(method,route,body,headers) with cookie persistence, returning {status,data,response,cookie}. All paths omit /api/v1 when using the helper. Always close in finally. CLI tests use async child processes so the HTTP event loop remains live.

Each lane owns its feature checks in scripts/checks/<lane>.mjs with export async smoke(ctx) and restart(ctx). Acceptance ctx contains {request,clients,ids,dataDir,url,check,cli}; checks must use public HTTP and actual CLI, save ids to ctx.ids without credentials in reports. The lead integrates these actual checks into acceptance modes. Public API docs are lane-specific docs/api-people.md, api-work.md, api-insight.md.

People's implemented service and shared outbox schema are specified in [People API](api-people.md). Use assertion methods on every protected route, and filter list queries with projectIds before pagination for guests. Public health/signup/login routes do not require an account; all current protected auth/people/SSE handlers check the shared service. The people.3 review and HTTP proofs cover integrated work routes through sprints and streamed attachments; insight remains a later integration audit. Credential-bearing account outbox links are browser-session only. See the People API current audit boundary.

People migrations 101 and 102 extend the existing auth spine with invitations/password reset hashes, personal API token hashes and sanitized security_audit. Purpose-bound HMAC credential verification uses CREW_SECRET before hashed database lookup; changing the secret invalidates all earlier credentials. No second user, session or outbox implementation exists. Security audit subscribes during people registration and registers its unsubscribe in ctx.cleanups. Password change retains only the caller's current browser session; reset invalidates every session and API token. Personal tokens cannot mint scopes broader than the caller's token. CLI groups may expose a handler.help string for credential-free --help; existing group help remains compatible.
